text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fears of a Mexican-style currency devaluation of the Thai baht swept through stock markets in Southeast Asia, sparking a storm of panic-selling among investors.
- The Singapore government is to cut the foreign worker levies it charges the manufacturing sector -- a surprise move welcomed by businesses.

- The proposed electric train service from Johor Baru to Tanjong Pagar in Singapore has been scrapped because of disagreement with the Singapore government over the positioning of cables, Malaysian Transport Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ling Liong Sik said.
- A computer programmer from Osaka flew to Singapore just to take Singapore Airlines inaugural Jubilee 777 flight to Jakarta.
- A 16-year-old boy will spend at least two years at the Singapore Boys' Home for having a pack of cigarettes, the fourth time he was caught for being an underaged smoker.

- Many baht speculators were hit as Bank of Thailand jacked up financing costs for currency punters, while regional central banks intervened jointly to defend the embattled currency for the second consecutive day.
- Kwek Leng Beng's London-listed Millennium and Copthorne Hotels (M&C) will spend Singapore $86.9 million to develop a 290-bedroom hotel on a historic site in Manchester, England.
- The Philippine monetary authorities raised overnight interest rates twice and sold about US$150 million as they tried to defend the peso against speculative attacks.

- Regional stocks came under heavy attack by speculators preying on worries that Thailand's shaky financial position could see a repeat of the Mexican crisis two years ago which battered emerging markets as far away as Southeast Asia.
- The Indonesian government is planning to accelerate the controversial national car project by roping in two leading domestic automakers, PT Astra International and PT Indomobil.
- The Bank of Thailand and its Asian central bank partners emerged the clear victors in the battle to defend the baht, but analysts say that the war against speculators may not be over yet.
- Mainboard-listed Lim Kah Ngam is selling its hotel-cum-supermarket project in Joo Chiat and most probably Hotel Equatorial to raise funds for new property projects.
- Tye Soon's initial public offering is believed to have been more than 60 times subscribed, garnering an above average response among IPOs issued this year.
- Poh Lian Holdings bucked the market trend on its stockmarket debut, closing at 51.5 cents, a respectable premium of 22.6 percent over its 42 cent offer price.
- Wire and cable maker Huan Hsin Holdings has received approval in principle for a U.S dollar-listing on the mainboard of the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
